plan.title: The Weight of Echoes
plan.premise: Deep beneath the Thornveil Marches, the death-song of a slain titan leaks upward through the stone, and everything that hears it remembers a life it never lived. Slendee and El'Skalfidar are drawn toward three sources of that song—each louder than the last—until they must choose whether to silence the last echo or let it finish remembering.
plan.tone: Melancholy wonder with teeth; grief made manifest in stone, tide, and fire.
plan.theme: What the dead leave behind keeps singing.

acts.title: The Hollow Toll
acts.goal: Trace the faint death-song to its first source and quiet the Gale Abbey bell that tolls with a voice not its own.

region.name: Thornveil Marches
region.flavour: A damp expanse of sunken lanes and elder forest where the soil hums faintly at dusk. Villagers bind bells to their wrists to drown out a low, wordless melody that only a few admit to hearing.

arrival.name: Dusk Hollow
arrival.flavour: A village of leaning slate roofs and hanging bell-charms that chime against each other without wind.

spokes.name: Keenmoss Bridge
spokes.flavour: A stone span over black water; the moss on its keystone pulses like a slow heartbeat.

spokes.name: Scabroot Cave
spokes.flavour: A low cave mouth exhaling warm air that smells of old pennies and wet hide.

spokes.name: Bleakfen Shrine
spokes.flavour: A slumped stone shrine at the marsh edge, its saint's face weathered smooth and weeping moss.

gateway.name: Gale Abbey
gateway.flavour: A roofless abbey whose single bronze bell rings itself at the turning of each hour, though no rope hangs from it.

boss.name: Brother Molt
boss.ally_path: Molt is not evil—he insists the bell is a choir, not a wound. If the party proves a second, truer source exists beyond his abbey, he will abandon the bell and aid them, lamenting his years of devotion to an echo.

acts.title: The Tide That Remembers
acts.goal: Cross the drowned lowlands and still the second source of the song, a thing that sings through every reed and ripple of the Gloomfen.

region.name: Gloomfen Wetlands
region.flavour: A brackish backwater of drowned orchards and slow channels where reflections lag a half-second behind the thing that casts them.

arrival.name: Rookwade Hollow
arrival.flavour: Stilt huts and fish-racks crouched over still brown water; the ferryman's pole strikes the mud with a sound like a struck tuning fork.

spokes.name: Sorrow Runnel
spokes.flavour: A narrow channel so choked with pale reeds it seems to be combing them with its current.

spokes.name: Drenwatch Ruins
spokes.flavour: Sunken watchtowers whose upper floors still break the surface, doors ajar like open mouths above the marsh.

spokes.name: Mirkfall Thicket
spokes.flavour: A grove of half-drowned trees whose bark is split by the shapes of faces not carved there.

gateway.name: The Sunken Choir
gateway.flavour: A ring of standing stones nearly swallowed by the fen, humming so low the water trembles in place.

boss.name: Raveth, the Half-Heard
boss.ally_path: Raveth was hatched in the titan's rib-cage and has only ever known its song as a lullaby. If the party speaks to it instead of striking, and offers a melody of their own in trade, it may relent and lead them to the true source—for it, too, is tired of singing alone.

acts.title: The Last Echo
acts.goal: Descend to the titan's buried breast and decide whether to end the death-song or let it finish its final verse.

region.name: The Under-Hymn
region.flavour: A vast subterranean sea-cave where the titan's fossil ribs curve overhead like the beams of a sunken cathedral, and the song is now loud enough to feel as pressure behind the eyes.

arrival.name: Voxmere Landing
arrival.flavour: A shelf of black limestone above an underground lake; the water's surface is glass-calm and faintly luminous with drifting motes.

spokes.name: The Ribbed Nave
spokes.flavour: A cavern whose ceiling is the titan's own ribcage, each bone broad enough to walk along and humming with stored song.

spokes.name: Ashensilt Crypts
spokes.flavour: Tombs of an elder people built between the titan's collapsed fingers, their doors all standing open inward.

spokes.name: The Echoing Mere
spokes.flavour: A warm black pool that replays the last moments of the titan's death in ripples that do not move at the party's touch.

gateway.name: The Still Heart
gateway.flavour: The titan's hollow chest, where a single stone heart the size of a chapel hangs suspended and slowly, silently cracks.

boss.name: Korvell, the Echo-Bearer
boss.ally_path: Korvell is the last living giant to have known the titan, and he lingers as its unwilling keeper. He will stand aside only if the party proves they do not seek to steal the song—by returning to him a smooth river-stone lost from his hand, found in the Echoing Mere.

npcs.name: Yeva Mossbell
npcs.demeanor: Tired, gentle, quick to touch a charm at her wrist.
npcs.motive: She hears the song in her sleep and wants it to stop without anyone dying.

secrets.text: Yeva has begun to hear her own late mother's voice inside the death-song, and part of her does not want it silenced.

npcs.name: Old Carrion Vess
npcs.demeanor: Laconic, patient, fond of rotten jokes.
npcs.motive: He ferries because the song quiets when he is over deep water.

secrets.text: Vess once rowed a drowned man's body to the Sunken Choir as an offering and has been haunted by the man's face ever since.

npcs.name: Priest Norven Hale
npcs.demeanor: Pious, guarded, keeps his hands behind his back.
npcs.motive: He believes the song is a divine test and that failing to endure it means damnation.

secrets.text: Norven has hidden a smooth river-stone carved with a giant's rune beneath the shrine altar, taken long ago from the Still Heart.

npcs.name: Mistress Kree the Ragged
npcs.demeanor: Sharp, wary, talks to her own shadow.
npcs.motive: She wants the song's power for herself to regrow the drowned forest.

secrets.text: Kree once planted a cutting in the titan's own soil and has been slowly turning toward stone from the wrist up.

npcs.voice_tag: lists plants by the hum they

npcs.name: Warden Sellen Ost
npcs.demeanor: Formal, weary, honor-bound to a fault.
npcs.motive: She swore to silence the song but cannot bring herself to enter the caves alone.

secrets.text: Sellen's company was swallowed by the Echoing Mere, and only she crawled out; she blames herself for their deaths.

npcs.name: Brindt
npcs.motive: He seeks the titan's heartstone to settle a debt that would destroy his clan.

secrets.text: Brindt already sold the location of the heart to a rival and now hopes the party destroys it before the buyer arrives.

quests.title: A Bell's False Tongue
quests.objective: Climb Gale Abbey and muffle the self-ringing bell so Dusk Hollow can sleep a full night.

quests.title: The Ferrystones
quests.objective: Recover three lost keystones from Keenmoss Bridge before the next flood tugs the span into the marsh.

quests.title: The Man in the Runnel
quests.objective: Search Sorrow Runnel for the remains of a drowned man Vess once ferried, and give them proper burial.

quests.title: A Shrine's False Saint
quests.objective: Drive the cult from Bleakfen Shrine and reclaim the altar before they finish their rites.

quests.title: Roots Over Water
quests.objective: Plant a living cutting at the edge of the Sunken Choir and return without touching the standing stones.

quests.title: The Knight's Penance
quests.objective: Recover her company's standard from Drenwatch Ruins and burn it properly so their oaths are released.

quests.title: The Weight of the Heart
quests.objective: Reach the Still Heart and take a single shard of the cracking heartstone—only enough to settle Brindt's debt—without waking the keeper.

event.text: Dusk Hollow gathers in a fold of damp ground, its slate roofs leaning together as though trading secrets. Bell-charms hang from every eave and post, knocking softly against one another though no wind stirs the air. The soil underfoot hums faintly, and the smell of wet moss and old rain settles over everything.

Yeva watches you both with the tired patience of someone who has already rung every bell in Dusk Hollow twice. The offered errands settle over the village like a stale hush, each task half-spoken and waiting to be taken up. Nothing moves to stop you, and the path remains open in three directions.

summary.text: Yeva watches you both with the tired patience of someone who has already rung every bell in Dusk Hollow twice.

event.text: You are at Dusk Hollow. Dusk Hollow gathers in a fold of damp ground, its slate roofs leaning together as though trading secrets. Bell-charms hang from every eave and post, knocking softly against one another though no wind stirs the air. The soil underfoot hums faintly, and the smell of wet moss and old rain settles over everything. Here with you: Yeva Mossbell (bell-warden of Dusk Hollow). Ways on: Keenmoss Bridge, Scabroot Cave and Bleakfen Shrine.

Yeva offers you a thin, weary nod, then her fingers find the little charm at her wrist once, twice. "Ah. You've come to talk, then. Good—too many folk just stand at the edge and stare, as if the bells might bite."

Yeva nods slowly and tells you the bell-tongue is a false relic that rings only for wicked ends. She asks if you would silence it at Bleakfen Shrine. Yeva Mossbell considers your words, but says nothing more for now.
Yeva gestures toward the distant shrine and says you will find the false tongue hidden among the votive rows, guarded by the shrine’s hushed shadows and its grave-quiet mercy.

Bleakfen Shrine slumps at the marsh edge, its saint's face weathered smooth and weeping moss. Black water seeps between broken stones, and the air hangs thick with rot and wet earth. Beneath the fen's slow sigh, a low hum trembles through the reeds.

The reeds part with a wet whisper and a stirge drops from its perch, wings buzzing as it wheels toward you. Slendee’s hand is already up, and the burst of eldritch light catches it mid-flight, sending it tumbling into the black water. The moment settles, and the scene waits on your next move.

summary.text: At Dusk Hollow, Yeva Mossbell met the party with the worn patience of one who has rung every bell twice, and told them the bell-tongue is a false relic that rings only for wicked ends. She asked them to silence it at Bleakfen Shrine, saying the false tongue is hidden among the votive rows, guarded by the shrine's hushed shadows and grave-quiet mercy. The party then travelled to Bleakfen Shrine, where a stirge dropped from the reeds; Slendee loosed eldritch light that caught it mid-flight and tumbled it into the black water. A low hum still trembles through the reeds, and the scene waits on the party's next move.
summary.title: A false tongue promised at Bleakfen

The false tongue lies hidden among the votive rows at Bleakfen Shrine, watched over by the shrine's hushed shadows and grave-quiet mercy.
Slendee struck down a stirge at Bleakfen Shrine with a burst of eldritch light, dropping it into the black water.
The party reached Bleakfen Shrine from Dusk Hollow; further ways lead to Gale Abbey (locked).

event.text: You slip forward through the reeds before the stirge can fix its hungry eyes on you, and the black water holds its breath. Slendee pulls it off, and the Stealth attempt succeeds. El’Skalfidar pulls it off, and the Stealth attempt succeeds. Weapons are drawn: a fight breaks out! Stirge is now surprised.

A second stirge darts from the reeds, drawn by the splash of the first. El’Skalfidar strikes Stirge. Stirge falls and does not rise again. The last foe falls, and the fight is won. The party grows more experienced. Priest Norven Hale's manner toward you shifts.

event.text: The priest regards you both from the step, hands still tucked behind his back. "Norven Hale," he says, "keeper of this shrine and keeper of its quiet."

event.reason: Convincing the guarded priest to guide the party to the hidden false bell-tongue

event.text: El’Skalfidar gives it everything, but the Persuasion attempt fails.

event.reason: Slendee threatens the priest to force information about the shrine's secret
Slendee threatened his life to force answers

event.text: The threat punches the air out of the step, and for a breath the priest just stares at Slendee. Then Norven Hale’s shoulders lower and one hand comes free, opening toward you both in a calm, empty gesture. “I hide what the shrine asks me to keep,” he says, his voice steadier now. “No good comes of killing its keeper.” "Even the stone cries out when the mire would have it silent," Norven says, his voice tight. "I hide only the shrine's quiet, and what offerings the fen-god spares."

event.reason: Carefully searching the shrine area for anything hidden

event.text: Slendee’s search pays off: among the votive rows, a thin tongue of false brass rests beneath a cloth the color of old moss. It glints only once, then stills, as though it knows it has been seen.

Norven Hale gives you both a long, measured look before answering: “Follow the boardwalk north through the reeds, and it will take you back toward Dusk Hollow. The path to the abbey is barred.” "The path behind you leads back to Dusk Hollow, if Dusk will still have you," Norven says, gesturing with one pale hand toward the reeds. "The abbey door is shut, and the fen keeps no finer road than the one that brought you."

feature.name: Gale Abbey Door
feature.description: A heavy barred door of black oak and rusted iron, sealing the way from Bleakfen Shrine toward Gale Abbey. The fen's damp has swollen the wood tight in its frame.

event.text: A spear of churning light leaps from Slendee’s hand and breaks against the abbey door. The black oak drinks the blast, and the iron bands ring like a struck bell, but the door stands sealed as ever.

event.reason: Examining the false brass bell-tongue found among the votive rows to discern its nature and any markings.

event.text: El’Skalfidar gives it everything, but the Investigation attempt fails.

keepsake.name: False Bell-Tongue
keepsake.description: A thin tongue of false brass, tarnished green with age, taken from beneath an old-moss cloth among the votive rows of Bleakfen Shrine. Cold to the touch, and it hums faintly, as if remembering a bell.

event.text: Slendee’s fingers close around the brass tongue, and the cloth of old moss falls away in a soft fold. The false relic rests in her grasp, cool and inert. It makes no sound.

event.reason: Examining the barred Gale Abbey door for weakness or mechanism

event.text: El’Skalfidar gives it everything, but the Investigation attempt fails.

event.reason: Examining the Gale Abbey Door closely for weaknesses, mechanisms, or detail.

fact.text: Slendee examines the Gale Abbey Door closely and finds the iron bands are bolted from the far side, and the damp-swollen oak will not yield to force alone — the lock mechanism sits behind the bars, unreachable from this side.

event.text: You run your hands along the swollen frame and peer beneath the iron bands. The lock sits behind the bars, untouched from this side, and the door’s weight has settled as if the fen itself leans against it. No seam, no give, no hidden catch; the abbey is sealed.

Norven’s eyes narrow on the brass tongue in Slendee’s hand. “That is no bell. It is the false tongue—the relic Yeva sent you to silence.” “A bell with no voice is a saint with no tongue,” Norven says, stepping nearer. “You hold a false thing — brass that would sing when it should keep silence. The fen-prayers call it a relic of a lying mouth.”

He looks toward the barred door and back to you. “Prayer may yet prove a better key than any thief’s tool.” “The door is swollen with the fen’s own grief, and the saint keeps her silence behind iron and oak.” Norven folds his hands behind his back. “I know no key that opens it from this side.”

Yeva Mossbell looks up from the charm at her wrist and says, “It means the relic never carried a saint’s voice—only ruin dressed in old bronze.”

Moss-caked stone arches over slow black water, its keystone pulsing faintly like a buried heart. Damp forest presses close on both banks, dripping and hushed, and the air tastes of wet bark and old rain. Beneath you the current slides by without a sound.

The bridge's moss-slick stones shift underfoot as a goblin peels itself from the shadows near the far arch, reed-knife already in hand. It watches you with wet, patient eyes, and the moment stretches thin.

The cave mouth exhales its coppery stink as you step inside, and the dark reshapes itself around a pair of quick, red eyes. A giant rat uncoils from the damp, watching you with bared teeth and no retreat. It waits at the edge of the black, deciding whether you are prey.

Windswept ruins sprawl across the hilltop, open to the sky where a roof once stood. Cold mist coils through broken arches, and the stone walls glisten, carrying the faint mineral scent of rain-soaked rock. Beneath your boots, the earth hums a deep, wordless melody.

Brother Molt plants himself in the Abbey’s broken arch before you can pass, his blocky shadow thrown long across the wet stone. Sellen Ost is at his shoulder, one gauntlet resting on her sword-hilt in weary habit. Neither speaks first. The wind drags through the gaps between them, and you hear the earth-hum rise under your boots. Molt’s stance leaves no path forward without a decision.

Brother Molt blocks the broken arch of Gale Abbey with Warden Sellen Ost at his shoulder, leaving no path forward without a decision.
Warden Sellen Ost keeps one gauntlet on her sword-hilt in weary habit; neither she nor Molt speaks first.

event.text: Brother Molt’s shadow leans toward you across the broken arch, and his fists curl at his sides. Sellen Ost does not draw, but her gauntlet turns on the hilt with a faint rasp. The two of you stand just beyond the stone’s yawn, weapons ready, while the low earth-hum thickens between you like a second threshold. For one held breath, no one moves. Then Molt shifts his weight forward, and the space narrows.

event.text: El’Skalfidar gives it everything, but the Religion attempt fails. El’Skalfidar gives it everything, but the Persuasion attempt fails.

Brother Molt crumples at the arch’s edge, his shadow collapsing into the wet stone, and the earth-hum falters. Sellen Ost draws no steel, only steps back one pace, her gauntlet falling from the hilt. Slendee stands over the body while the Scroll of Sleep curls in her fingers. The moment settles, and the scene waits on your next move.

feature.description: A half-crumbled niche in the abbey wall, its stone cracked by time; something glints beneath a shard of fallen masonry.

event.text: Slendee’s search turns over little at first—chips of broken arch, dead moss—until her gaze catches a glint under a slab of fallen masonry in the wall niche. Kneeling closer, she makes out the shape beneath the stone: not treasure, but something long buried in shadow. The moment settles, and the scene waits on your next move.

Slendee steps toward Brother Molt with words ready, but his jaw sets like stone and whatever she meant to say falls flat against his silence. The arch stays barred. “Speak to Molt, then, but mind your words.”
The moment passes, and the world waits for what you do next.

Slendee’s eldritch light cracks against the barred door and sprays back along her arm in a hot, needling sting. She recoils, breath sharp, while the arch remains shut and Brother Molt watches in silence.
The moment passes, and the world waits for what you do next.

Slendee's crackling bolt flies wide of Warden Sellen Ost, splitting the damp air beside her shoulder and fading into the broken masonry beyond. The knight-at-large does not flinch; only her gauntlet tightens once on the sword-hilt, and her weary eyes settle on Slendee with cold finality. Brother Molt drags himself upright in the arch's shadow, and the low hum in the earth climbs again.

event.text: You stand in Rookwade Hollow, where stilt huts and fish-racks crouch low over still brown water that barely moves. The air hangs thick and damp, heavy with rot and silt, and every sound arrives slightly wrong, as if the swamp itself is listening. When the ferryman's pole strikes the mud, it rings out like a struck tuning fork, humming long after it should have faded.
The ferryman watches you arrive without shifting his weight on the pole. Water laps once against the nearest stilt and falls still.

summary.text: The party travelled to Rookwade Hollow and arrived among its stilt huts and fish-racks over still brown water. Old Carrion Vess, the ferryman and grave-digger, watched them arrive without shifting his weight on his pole. Water lapped once against the nearest stilt, then fell still.
summary.title: Arrival at Rookwade Hollow

fact.text: The party arrived at Rookwade Hollow, a settlement of stilt huts and fish-racks over still brown water.
Old Carrion Vess, the ferryman and grave-digger, was present at Rookwade Hollow and watched the party arrive without shifting his weight on his pole.
Rookwade Hollow opens onto three exits: Sorrow Runnel, Drenwatch Ruins and Mirkfall Thicket.

event.text: Old Carrion Vess taps his pole once against the boards and names a price that sounds less like a fare and more like a tax on curiosity. He waits. "Passage costs what the water asks, and the water don't always ask coin." He shifts his grip on the pole without looking at you. "Could be a favor. Could be a fetch. Could be you sit a while so the mud can settle."

event.text: Old Carrion Vess takes the brass bell from Slendee's hand, turns it so the false tongue catches the dull light, and tucks it into a fold of his coat. "That'll do," he says, "for one crossing, when you're ready."

You stand in the Gloomfen Wetlands at Sorrow Runnel, where brackish water threads between drowned orchards. The channel narrows until its current combs through walls of reeds that hiss and whisper against the flow. Beneath a sagging bridge, black water slides without sound, and the whole marsh stinks of rot and iron.

The reeds at Sorrow Runnel whisper as you step onto the bank, and the black water slides past without sound. The sagging bridge looms ahead, its timbers dark and slick. A pallid shape stirs from the muck near the far arch, and the air turns cold with a grave-stink. Slendee readies herself as the ghast uncurls from the reeds.

summary.text: At Rookwade Hollow, Old Carrion Vess tapped his pole and set a crossing price that might be coin, a favour or a fetch, then took Slendee's brass bell and tucked it into his coat as payment for one crossing. The party then travelled to Sorrow Runnel, where a pallid ghast uncurled from the muck near the far arch beneath the sagging bridge, filling the air with grave-stink. Slendee readied herself as the black water slid past in silence, and nothing is yet resolved between the party and the ghast.

Mirkfall Thicket stands as a drowned grove within the Gloomfen Wetlands, where black water pools between the roots of half-submerged trees. Their bark splits into the shapes of anguished faces, though no blade has ever carved them. The air hangs thick with rot and damp, and every sound you make returns to you a half-second late.

A green wyrmling drops from the low branches like a knot of old leaves, its breath already hissing through the dark. You are the first thing it sees; the water underneath you lies still as your choice forms. Slendee remains limp and useless at your side, her weight a dead anchor against your shoulder.

event.text: Old Carrion Vess lets his gaze drift over your open gear and says only, "The water's already taken its price from you." Vess lets his gaze drift over what you show, then taps the pole once against the mud. "Water don't buy much from the living." A pause, as if listening. "But it might take that longbow for a crossing, if you've nowhere to be."
The moment passes, and the world waits for what you do next.
Old Carrion Vess does not reach for the bow. He shakes his head once and lets it rest against the mud, as if the wood is no better than a stone of the hollow.

keepsake.description: A tarnished silver token, punched with a rook, pulled unnoticed from Old Carrion Vess's coat. It is the sort of coin the dead are given for passage.

event.text: Your fingers find the ferryman’s coat lighter than expected, and the grave-silver ferryl slides free without so much as a shift in his weight. Old Carrion Vess does not turn, and the water keeps its secret. Old Carrion Vess lets the silence hang a breath too long, then shifts his grip on the pole. "Hands that quick often find what the water's already given up." His eyes drift past you toward the black channel. "Mind it don't ask twice."
Your prayer to the scribe rises through the damp air and finds only the ferryman’s silence, as if the words are swallowed by the water before they can settle anywhere.
Your fingers close on Slendee’s coin, but the ferryman’s gaze finds you before the purse does. The water swallows the gesture and gives nothing back.
